case-1.objects: A real Hilbert space E with its Borel measurable structure, a measure μ on E, and a real-valued function f on E. Write ∇ for the Hilbert gradient (the Riesz representative of the Fréchet derivative), χ_R for radialSmoothCutoff R, and R_n = (n : ℝ) + 1. The fixed approximation is f_n(x) = χ_{R_n}(x) f(x).
case-1.domains: x ranges over all of E, n ranges over ℕ including 0, and the cutoff radius is real (each R_n ≥ 1). f, f_n, the integrands, the integral values, and their limits are real-valued; the gradients take values in E and use its Hilbert norm. All integrals are over E against the same μ.
case-1.quantifiers: For every implicit type E equipped with the displayed structures, every measure μ on E and every f : E → ℝ satisfying the premises, the three limits hold along the same sequence indexed by ℕ. Equivalently, for each ε > 0 there is an N ∈ ℕ such that, for all n ≥ N, each of the three integral values differs from its stated limit by less than ε. No uniformity in E, μ, or f is required, and there is no quantification over alternative cutoff families or radius sequences.
case-1.assumptions: E is a normed additive commutative group with a real inner product, is complete, and has a measurable structure equal to the Borel σ-algebra. f is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable on all of E, f and ∇f belong to L²(μ), and x ↦ f(x)² log(f(x)²) is absolutely integrable against μ. The L² and integrability conditions include a.e. strong measurability. There is no assumption of finite dimension or separability, no finiteness, probability normalization, σ-finiteness or absolute-continuity condition on μ, and no boundedness, support, nonvanishing, or Hessian-integrability condition on f.
case-1.conclusion: As n → ∞, the following three real scalar convergences hold jointly: ∫_E f_n(x)² dμ(x) → ∫_E f(x)² dμ(x); ∫_E f_n(x)² log(f_n(x)²) dμ(x) → ∫_E f(x)² log(f(x)²) dμ(x); and ∫_E ‖∇f_n(x)‖² dμ(x) → ∫_E ‖∇f(x)‖² dμ(x).
case-1.senses: Each Tendsto is from atTop on ℕ to the usual real neighborhood filter of its stated integral. The integrals are real Lebesgue/Bochner integrals; the logarithmic integrand is signed and uses the continuous extension q log q = 0 at q = 0 for q ≥ 0. It is not a normalized entropy or a KL divergence. The conclusion asserts convergence of the three integral values, not pointwise, uniform, or L² convergence of f_n or ∇f_n as separate claims. It does not assert a rate, an entropy inequality, or compact support (closed bounded balls need not be compact here).
case-1.constants: The cutoff is smooth and radial about 0, lies in [0,1], is identically 1 on the closed ball of radius R, and is supported in the closed ball of radius 2R. For R > 0 its first Fréchet derivative has operator norm bounded by C/R with C independent of R and x; no value of C is specified or occurs in the limits. Here R is fixed to n + 1, so the two radii are n + 1 and 2(n + 1). The differentiability order is 2 and both Lᵖ exponents and the displayed squares use 2.
